purpose: Epoprostenol is used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), which is high blood pressure in the arteries that carry blood to your lungs. It helps make it easier for your heart to pump blood and allows you to breathe and exercise more comfortably. It is also sometimes used during certain heart and kidney procedures.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes a substance called prostacyclin that helps relax and widen blood vessels. Epoprostenol works like that natural substance by relaxing and opening up the blood vessels in your lungs, so blood can flow through more easily. It also helps prevent blood cells from clumping together, which reduces the risk of dangerous clots forming.
common_side_effects: Flushing or redness of the face, headache, jaw pain especially when eating, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dizziness, low blood pressure, and muscle or joint pain. These are fairly common and your care team will help manage them.
warnings: This medication is given through a continuous IV infusion using a small pump you carry with you — it must NEVER be stopped suddenly, as this can cause a dangerous and potentially life-threatening drop in blood pressure. Keep backup supplies and pump batteries on hand at all times. The medication must be prepared carefully and kept cold. Infections at the IV site are a serious risk, so strict cleanliness is very important. Tell your doctor right away if you have chest pain, sudden shortness of breath, or feel faint.
typical_dosing: Epoprostenol is given as a continuous drip directly into a vein (IV) through a special long-term central line, 24 hours a day, every day. Your doctor will start you on a very low dose and slowly increase it over time based on how you feel and how well you tolerate it. The dose is always customized to each individual patient and managed closely by your healthcare team.
